title: Usage ledger reconciliation and tamper-evident audit snapshot procedures
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Purpose: Define and implement a repeatable, tamper-evident reconciliation and snapshotting process for usage events that will be the canonical evidence for billing invoices and SOC-style audits. Background: Current metering pipeline emits events to Kafka, which are processed into aggregated token counts. We need an append-only usage ledger, daily reconciliations, signed snapshots, and a documented playbook for auditors to verify billing correctness without exposing PII. This ticket delivers the implementation plan, runbooks, schema, queries, test plan, and the artifact package format for audit evidence.
acceptance_criteria: An append-only usage ledger export is produced daily and contains all resolved usage events for the day (ingest -> enrichment -> charges), with sequence numbers and hash chaining for tamper evidence
A reconciliation job runs within 2 hours of UTC day boundary producing a human-readable CSV + machine-signed bundle (SHA256 + KMS signature) stored in s3://redwood-audit/ledger-snapshots/YYYY-MM-DD/
Automated reconciliation validates ledger totals against billing aggregation tables and raises alerts if variance > 0.1% or absolute delta > $100
Runbook exists describing steps for auditors to verify snapshot integrity (hash chain check, signature validation, aggregated totals check) and is linked in Confluence
Access controls: only billing-admin and compliance roles can read raw snapshots; a redacted-view for internal finance is available; access is logged and retention policy is enforced
tasks: Design ledger event schema (event_id, seq, ts, customer_id_hash, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_units, rate_plan_id, rate_id, source_cluster)
Implement append-only ledger writer in metering service with monotonic seq and prev_hash chaining
Build daily snapshot generator that composes CSV, computes Merkle root and signs with KMS key 'billing-signer-2025'
Add reconciliation job comparing ledger aggregates vs billing_aggregates table and emit discrepancy metrics to Datadog and alerts to PagerDuty
Create Confluence runbook and audit artifact README with verification commands
Add IAM policies and S3 bucket policy for snapshot storage and integrate with audit logging
log_schema: Event ledger schema (CSV headers): event_id, seq, ts_utc, customer_id_hash, account_id_hash, product_family, model_name, model_variant, request_type, tokens_input, tokens_output, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost_units, rate_plan_id, rate_id, zone, ingest_cluster, processor_version, prev_hash, event_hash. Each record is hashed (SHA256) and prev_hash links to previous seq to form tamper-evident chain. Sensitive IDs are stored as salted HMAC hashes using KMS-derived salt before writing to ledger.
retention_policy: Raw signed snapshots: immutable copies retained for 7 years (compliance requirement). Working intermediate state (processing topics, temp exports): 90 days. Access logs and auditor downloads: 3 years. Implementation detail: lifecycle policies on s3://redwood-audit to transition to Glacier after 1 year. Deletion of keys: rotation schedule for KMS signer key and archival of old keys per security policy.
reconciliation_runbook:
Primary reconciliation flow:
1) After UTC 00:00+2h window, trigger reconciliation job 'ledger-reconcile-YYYY-MM-DD'.
2) Job pulls ledger slice for date, computes per-account totals and compares to billing_aggregates table.
3) If checksums match, package CSV, compute Merkle root and sign bundle with KMS; upload to s3 under 'ledger-snapshots/DATE/signed-bundle.zip' and write metadata to audit index table.
4) If variance detected: open incident, label 'billing-reconciliation-variance', collect debug artifacts (raw events for 2-hour window, enrichment logs, rate table snapshot), notify finance + oncall SRE.
5) For manual auditor verification, provide verification script: verify_signature.sh, verify_chain.py, and summary.json with totals per account.
verification_commands: # Verify KMS signature: aws kms verify --key-id alias/billing-signer-2025 --message fileb://bundle.csv --signature fileb://bundle.sig
# Compute and verify Merkle root: python3 tools/verify_merkle.py --input bundle.csv --expected-root <root-from-metadata.json>
# Quick totals check: psql -c "SELECT account_hash, SUM(cost_units) FROM billing_aggregates WHERE date='YYYY-MM-DD' GROUP BY 1;"
test_plan: Unit tests for ledger writer: sequence monotonicity, prev_hash correctness, salted hash format
Integration test: end-to-end ingestion -> ledger write -> snapshot -> signature verification in CI using test KMS stub
Chaos test: drop 1% of meter events in staging and assert reconciliation flags variance and triggers incident path
Load test: ensure ledger writer can sustain 10k events/sec on the busiest cluster during synthetic replay
Audit walkthrough: internal compliance team runs verification commands and signs off on artifact format
audit_artifact_format: Bundle (signed-bundle.zip) contents: ledger.csv (canonical CSV), metadata.json (date, merkle_root, signer_key_id, version), bundle.sig (KMS signature of ledger.csv), summary.csv (aggregated totals per account/product), README.md (verification steps). All files are UTF-8 and newline-separated. Metadata.json intentionally contains no raw PII; customer identifiers are hashed.
access_controls: Principle of least privilege. IAM roles: billing-admin (can LIST and GET snapshots, perform verifications), compliance-auditor (read-only), finance-analyst (redacted-view via Athena view that masks customer_id_hash), infra-ops (write-only for reconciliation job). S3 bucket policy denies public access and requires AWS:SecureTransport. All access is logged to CloudTrail with log entries forwarded to an immutable logging bucket and to the SIEM. Requests to download snapshots require a signed justification ticket recorded in the audit-index table.
incident_playbook: If reconciliation job fails or variance > thresholds: 1) PagerDuty oncall SRE receives alert and acknowledges within 15m. 2) Attach reconciliation job logs and raw ledger slice to incident. 3) Triage: check for replays, consumer lag, enrichment failures, or pricing table migrations. 4) If root cause is missing events, schedule targeted replay from Kafka with idempotent write guard; run isolated reconciliation on replayed range. 5) Communicate customer-facing impact via finance only if variance affects invoices beyond dispute thresholds.
